title: A length is a specified pair of events
question: Which endpoint measurements define a moving rod’s length?
recap: A moving rod’s length uses endpoint positions measured at the same time in the measuring frame. Transforming a pair simultaneous in another frame usually does not produce that measurement.
premises: The rod moves inertially along the boost axis with a fixed rest length.
Each frame uses its own synchronized clocks.
limitations: Coordinate length is not the appearance in a photograph.
Comparing different event pairs is essential, not an optional correction.

overview.text: A moving rod’s length uses endpoint positions measured at the same time in the measuring frame. Transforming a pair simultaneous in another frame usually does not produce that measurement.

full.text: A ruler traveling with the rod measures its rest length. An observer past whom it moves must record both endpoint positions simultaneously in that observer’s frame. Using one endpoint now and the other later includes part of the rod’s motion.
For the standard frame change, two event differences obey the same Lorentz map as coordinates. A pair with Δt = 0 and nonzero Δx generally has nonzero Δt′.

full.spoken: Events simultaneous in the unprimed frame have a primed time difference of minus gamma v delta x over c squared.

full.text: In SR-03, select a simultaneous slice and inspect the endpoint event identities. A larger transformed separation from an unsuitable pair does not mean the moving rod has become longer.

full.returnCaption: Return to which endpoint measurements define a moving rod’s length.

items: Choose the frame in which the length is to be measured.
Choose the same coordinate time for its two endpoint events.
Subtract their positions in that frame.
When changing frame, transform the event times as well as positions.
Select a new simultaneous pair in the other frame before calling a separation its measured length.

margin.text: The map used to explain this difference is derived in §3. Its preview here anticipates that result rather than claiming a derivation from the §2 measurement description alone.
